L3: # apcore-a2a (Python) L4: L5: [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/apcore-a2a)](https://pypi.org/project/apcore-a2a/) L6: [![Python](https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/apcore-a2a)](https://pypi.org/project/apcore-a2a/) L7: [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE) L8: [![Coverage](https://img.shields.io/badge/coverage-90%25-brightgreen)](https://github.com/aiperceivable/apcore-a2a-python) L9: ## What is apcore-a2a? L10: L11: **apcore-a2a** is the [A2A (Agent-to-Agent)](https://google.github.io/A2A/) protocol adapter for the [apcore](https://github.com/aiperceivable/apcore-python) ecosystem. L12: It solves a common problem: **you've built AI capabilities with apcore modules, but you need them to talk to other AI agents over a standard protocol.** apcore-a2a bridges that gap — it reads your existing module metadata (schemas, descriptions, examples) and automatically exposes them as a standards-compliant A2A server. No hand-written Agent Cards, no JSON-RPC boilerplate, no manual task lifecycle management. L13: **In short:** `apcore modules` + `apcore-a2a` = a fully functional A2A agent, ready to be discovered and invoked by any A2A-compatible client. L14: L15: > **Also available in:** [TypeScript](https://github.com/aiperceivable/apcore-a2a-typescript) | [Rust](https://github.com/aiperceivable/apcore-a2a-rust) L16: ## Features L17: - **One-call server** — launch a compliant A2A server with `serve(registry)` L18: - **Automatic Agent Card** — `/.well-known/agent-card.json` generated from module metadata (the 0.3 alias `/.well-known/agent.json` is also served) L19: - **Skill mapping** — apcore modules become A2A Skills with names, descriptions, tags, and examples; `metadata["display"]["a2a"]` overrides surface-facing fields (§5.13) L20: - **Full task lifecycle** — submitted, working, completed, failed, canceled, input-required L21: - **SSE streaming** — `message/stream` with real-time status and artifact updates L22: - **Push notifications** — optional webhook delivery of task state changes L23: - **JWT authentication** — tokens bridged to apcore's Identity context L24: - **A2A Explorer UI** — browser UI for discovering and testing skills L25: - **Built-in client** — `A2AClient` for calling remote A2A agents L26: - **Pluggable storage** — swap in Redis or PostgreSQL via the `TaskStore` protocol L27: - **Observability** — `/health`, `/metrics` endpoints, structured logging L28: - **Dynamic registration** — add/remove modules at runtime without restart L29: ## Requirements L30: L31: - Python >= 3.11 L32: - `apcore` >= 0.32.0 L33: - `apcore-toolkit` >= 0.14.0 (the `openapi` extra additionally needs `apcore-toolkit[http-proxy]`) L34: L35: --- L36: L37: ## For Users: Getting Started L38: L39: ### Installation L40: L41: ```bash L42: pip install apcore-a2a L43: ``` L44: ### Expose your modules as an A2A Agent L45: L46: If you already have apcore modules, a few lines turn them into a discoverable agent: L47: L48: ```python L49: from apcore import Executor, Registry L50: from apcore_a2a import serve L51: L52: registry = Registry(extensions_dir="./extensions") L53: registry.discover() L54: L55: serve(Executor(registry)) # Starts on http://0.0.0.0:8000 L56: ``` L57: L58: Your agent is now live at `http://localhost:8000/.well-known/agent-card.json` (the 0.3 alias `/.well-known/agent.json` is also served). L59: ### Serve an OpenAPI document instead L60: L61: No apcore project required — point it at an OpenAPI 3.0/3.1 document and every operation L62: becomes an A2A Skill, proxied over HTTP to the API that published it: L63: L64: ```bash L65: pip install "apcore-a2a[openapi]" L66: L67: apcore-a2a serve --from-openapi https://petstore3.swagger.io/api/v3/openapi.json \ L68: --openapi-prefix petstore L69: ``` L70: L71: Or programmatically: L72: L73: ```python L74: from apcore_a2a import openapi_backend, serve L75: registry = openapi_backend( L76: "https://petstore3.swagger.io/api/v3/openapi.json", L77: prefix="petstore", L78: ) L79: serve(registry) L80: ``` L81: Each skill's ID is the module ID apcore-toolkit (>= 0.13) derives, already in apcore's ID L82: alphabet: `operationId: listPets` under prefix `petstore` becomes `petstore.list_pets`, and L83: `GET /pets/{petId}` without an `operationId` becomes `petstore.pets.pet_id.get`. An operation L84: whose ID still has a segment beginning with a digit (`/v1/2fa`) is skipped with a warning — L85: name it with a `derive_module_id` or `transform_module` hook. L86: > [!WARNING] L87: > An OpenAPI document describes an API's *shape*, not the *consequences* of calling it, so L88: > `requires_approval` is never inferred — a `POST /charges` that moves money is annotated L89: > exactly like a `POST /echo`. Such an operation is therefore advertised on the **public** L90: > Agent Card, which is served without authentication. apcore-a2a warns about this at L91: > startup, and the warning is not silenced by merely attaching an ACL. L92: > L93: > The recommended shape is `--openapi-prefix` plus an ACL with `default_effect: deny` and a L94: > prefixed catch-all deny rule; see [the feature spec][openapi-backend] for why an L95: > allow-list of operation names is the fail-safe direction when an upstream API renames L96: > something. L97: [openapi-backend]: https://github.com/aiperceivable/apcore-a2a/blob/main/docs/features/openapi-backend.md L98: ### Try the Examples L99: L100: Run all 5 example modules (3 class-based + 2 binding YAML) with the Explorer UI: L101: L102: ```bash L103: PYTHONPATH=./examples/binding_demo python examples/run.py L104: ``` L105: L106: Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/explorer/ to browse skills, send messages, and stream responses. L107: L108: See [`examples/README.md`](examples/README.md) for more options (CLI, binding-only, JWT auth). L109: ### Call a remote A2A Agent L110: L111: Use the built-in client to discover and invoke any A2A-compliant agent: L112: L113: ```python L114: import asyncio L115: from apcore_a2a import A2AClient L116: L117: async def main(): L118: async with A2AClient("http://remote-agent:8000") as client: L119: # Discover what the agent can do L120: card = await client.discover() L121: print(f"Agent: {card['name']}, Skills: {len(card['skills'])}") L122: # Send a message (route to a skill via metadata.skillId) L123: message = {"role": "user", "parts": [{"kind": "text", "text": "Hello!"}]} L124: task = await client.send_message( L125: message, L126: metadata={"skillId": "my.skill"}, L127: ) L128: print(f"Result: {task['status']['state']}") L129: L130: # Or stream the response L131: async for event in client.stream_message(message, metadata={"skillId": "my.skill"}): L132: print(event) L133: L134: asyncio.run(main()) L135: ``` L136: ### Add authentication L137: L138: ```python L139: from apcore_a2a import serve L140: from apcore_a2a.auth.jwt import JWTAuthenticator, ClaimMapping L141: L142: auth = JWTAuthenticator( L143: key="your-secret-key", L144: algorithms=["HS256"], L145: issuer="https://auth.example.com", L146: audience="my-agent", L147: claim_mapping=ClaimMapping( L148: id_claim="sub", L149: type_claim="type", L150: roles_claim="roles", L151: attrs_claims=["org", "dept"], L152: ), L153: require_claims=["sub"], L154: ) L155: L156: serve(registry, auth=auth) L157: ``` L158: L159: --- L160: ## For Developers: API Reference L161: ### `serve()` L162: L163: Blocking call — starts uvicorn and serves until SIGINT/SIGTERM. L164: L165: ```python L166: from apcore_a2a import serve L167: serve( L168: registry_or_executor, # apcore Registry or Executor L169: *, L170: host="0.0.0.0", L171: port=8000, L172: name=None, # Agent name (fallback: registry config) L173: description=None, # Agent description L174: version=None, # Agent version L175: url=None, # Public URL (default: f"http://{host}:{port}") L176: auth=None, # Authenticator instance L177: task_store=None, # TaskStore instance (default: InMemoryTaskStore) L178: cors_origins=None, # List of allowed CORS origins L179: push_notifications=False, L180: explorer=False, # Enable A2A Explorer UI L181: explorer_prefix="/explorer", L182: cancel_on_disconnect=True, L183: shutdown_timeout=30, L184: execution_timeout=300, L185: log_level=None, L186: metrics=False, # Enable /metrics endpoint L187: sys_modules=False, # Register apcore sys.* modules (requires executor.use()) L188: ) L189: ``` L190: ### `async_serve()` L191: L192: Returns the ASGI app without starting a server — use for embedding in larger applications. L193: L194: ```python L195: from apcore_a2a import async_serve L196: L197: app = await async_serve(registry_or_executor, **kwargs) L198: # app is a Starlette ASGI application L199: ``` L200: ### `TaskStore` L201: L202: Default in-memory task store. Implement the `TaskStore` protocol for persistent backends (Redis, PostgreSQL, etc.). L203: L204: ```python L205: from apcore_a2a.storage import InMemoryTaskStore L206: L207: store = InMemoryTaskStore() L208: serve(registry, task_store=store) L209: ``` L210: ### Architecture L211: L212: apcore-a2a acts as a thin protocol layer on top of apcore. The mapping is straightforward: L213: | A2A Concept | apcore Mapping | L214: | -------------- | ----------------------------------------- | L215: | **Agent Card** | Derived from Registry configuration | L216: | **Skill id** | `module_id` | L217: | **Skill name** | `metadata["display"]["a2a"]["alias"]` or humanized `module_id` | L218: | **Skill desc** | `metadata["display"]["a2a"]["description"]` or `module.description` | L219: | **Skill tags** | `metadata["display"]["tags"]` or `module.tags` | L220: | **Task** | Managed execution of `Executor.call_async()` | L221: | **Streaming** | Wrapped `Executor.stream()` via SSE | L222: | **Security** | Bridged to apcore's `Identity` context | L223: ### Contributing L224: L225: ```bash L226: git clone https://github.com/aiperceivable/apcore-a2a-python.git L227: cd apcore-a2a-python L228: pip install -e ".[dev]" L229: pytest L230: ``` L231: L232: ## Documentation L233: L234: - [Product Requirements (PRD)](https://github.com/aiperceivable/apcore-a2a/blob/main/docs/apcore-a2a/prd.md) -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Internal Error () 【turn453035view1】 [wordlim: 200] Source: open({"ref_id":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aiperceivable/apcore-a2a-python/c8b5ae5c15ae7e848cdfb45c2f063293d172061d/tests/test_executor.py","lineno":null});
